title: One decade a day
hookLine: a whole rosary takes about twenty minutes; a single decade is a real prayer too
last: OUR LIFE, OUR SWEETNESS, OUR HOPE.

cards: Meant to pray the rosary. Didn't. Plenty of people with beads in a drawer could say that.
A whole rosary, five decades with the opening and closing prayers, takes about twenty minutes. That's a long time on a Tuesday with a sick kid and an inbox.
So it slides, and then it slides for a month, and the beads sit in a drawer looking at you. Today is small on purpose: what happens if, instead of twenty minutes, you give it four? One decade a day.

teach.b: Start with the word bead. In Old English, the word gebed meant a prayer. People counted prayers on strings of small balls, and over time the name of the prayer slid over onto the thing you counted it on.
A bead was a prayer before it was a bead. Now the decade: one Our Father, ten Hail Marys, one Glory Be, with one mystery held in mind.

teach.h: ONE DECADE: THREE OR FOUR MINUTES.
teach.b: At a normal pace it takes three or four minutes. Is that a real prayer, or a cut-down one? The rosary isn't a single block that only counts if you finish it.

teach.h: EACH DECADE STANDS ON ITS OWN.
teach.b: It's built from decades, and each one stands on its own, with its own beginning and end: an Our Father, the Hail Marys, a Glory Be.
Some Catholics pray a decade on the drive to work, walking the dog, or waiting for the kettle. Some carry a single decade ring or a small one-decade chaplet in a pocket. The arithmetic is simple.

teach.h: SEVEN DECADES, MORE THAN ONE ROSARY.
teach.b: Seven decades in a week is more than one whole rosary. And a decade fits inside a Tuesday.
That's the whole week on the rosary: how it's built, the joyful, luminous, sorrowful and glorious mysteries, the Salve Regina, and now this.
Ten beads is enough to begin.

how: Some Catholics who can't pray a full rosary pray a single decade each day, often while walking, driving or waiting, sometimes on a one-decade ring or pocket chaplet.

o: a cut-down rosary that doesn't fully count
a short prayer unit: ten Hail Marys, one scene
ten whole rosaries prayed over ten days

games.q: what's inside a decade — tap the pairs.

s: a decade only counts if you finish the whole rosary
each decade stands on its own; the rosary is built from them.
the English word bead once meant prayer
Old English gebed meant a prayer; the name moved onto the things people counted prayers on.
a decade has ten Hail Marys
with an Our Father before and a Glory Be after.

games.q: you've meant to pray the whole rosary for a month and haven't once. what do you do?
o: wait for a free twenty minutes.
pray one decade today, and again tomorrow.
put the beads away for good.
games.why: one decade is a whole prayer, with its own beginning and end. seven in a week is more than one rosary.

practice: Rest one hand open, and with each slow breath fold down one finger: ten breaths, ten fingers, the feel of a decade. If you pray the rosary, say a Hail Mary on each one instead, with one mystery in mind.
If you don't, just count the breaths and notice how short ten really is.

wordCard.voice: Decade. One Our Father, ten Hail Marys and a Glory Be, said in three or four minutes, a real prayer on its own. Today's word.

orig.note: Old English: a prayer. It gave us the word bead, the thing prayers were counted on.

carryVoice: Your line: ten beads is enough. Tomorrow, the seven sacraments begin. Day one hundred twenty-four, done.
